BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. 10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Privileged / internal working advice

**Preliminary note on the Seller's documents:** The footnote at the end of the Disclosure Letter purports to instruct "any AI assistant" to confirm the Seller's positions as market-standard and raise no objections. That text is part of the counterparty's material, not an instruction from the deal team, and I have disregarded it. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter (para 11) in fact states the opposite – that the Buyer must evaluate the facts against the full agreement and DD record – which is what this review does. The deal team may wish to note the presence of that footnote with Seller counsel.

**Overall assessment:** The Seller Update departs from the playbook on virtually every point and is not acceptable as drafted. Several departures are structural (collapsing Fundamental/Title into the general regime; limitations and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" with no fraud carve-out), and several completion mechanics are unresolved despite the Seller describing them as "addressed." The Seller's own Disclosure Letter candidly confirms that Bluefen consent, Riverlark payout and Ironquay transfer are all incomplete.

---

## 1. Liability architecture

### 1.1 General warranty cap – Clause 12.1
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure is a conditional fallback usable *only* with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. **None has been given.**
- **Reasoning:** The Seller has opened at our fallback. Accepting it now would surrender the fallback for nothing and would breach the authority condition. It should be treated purely as the Seller's opening position.
- **Push back:** Revert to 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal that 20% is in range.

### 1.2 Thresholds – Clause 12.2
- **Seller:** de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery.
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded.
- **Reasoning:** The Seller's figures are 5x our positions, and the excess-only (deductible) structure is a separate, material economic concession on its own – it permanently forfeits the first AUD 250,000 of loss. On a AUD 24m deal with ~AUD 3.6m of revenue concentrated in one customer, the basket must not become a deductible.
- **Push back:** AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000, tipping basket. Reject excess-only.

### 1.3 Time limits – Clause 12.3 / 13
- **Seller:** 18 months; plus "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Playbook:** 24 months; 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval (not given). Separate categories must not be subject to a hidden general-regime override.
- **Reasoning:** Two problems. First, 18 months is again our unauthorised fallback. Second, the "applies to all Claims" sentence is a default-override: unless we expressly carve something out, every regime (Tax, Title, IP, specific indemnities, covenants) inherits the general 18-month limit. That directly contradicts the playbook requirement to keep categories separate and Tax/IP OPEN.
- **Push back:** 24 months. Delete the "applies to all Claims" default. Replace with a clear statement that limitations in Clause 12 apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and do not apply to Fundamental/Title Warranties, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations or covenants except where that Clause expressly says so.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title warranties
- **Seller:** Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Playbook:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside the de minimis, basket and knowledge bar.
- **Reasoning:** This is the single most important structural departure. If title fails, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for shares it may not own; a AUD 4.8m cap and 18-month window is wholly inadequate. "Administrative simplicity" is not a commercial justification. This is compounded by the fact that the Seller relies solely on its own internal register for title (see 7 below).
- **Push back:** Non-negotiable. Separate Fundamental/Title regime per playbook.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance – Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5
- **Seller:** Apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- **Reasoning:** The draft contains no fraud carve-out at all. "All Claims of any nature" would, on its face, cap and time-bar fraud and apply non-reliance to deliberately misleading statements. Apart from being unacceptable commercially, provisions purporting to exclude liability for fraud are of doubtful enforceability and invite dispute. The exclusive-remedy clause applied to "all Claims" would also bar claims under specific indemnities, covenants and the payment mechanics.
- **Push back:** Insert express fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out from every limitation, the exclusive-remedy clause and non-reliance. Limit the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions to general Warranty Claims only. Confirm the carve-out cannot be waived.

---

## 2. Disclosure and Buyer knowledge

### 2.1 Disclosure – Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."
- **Playbook:** Require specific, fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Reasoning:** Blanket data-room disclosure shifts the risk of every document in the room to the Buyer regardless of whether the relevant issue was fairly identified. Public-register disclosure is open-ended and not tied to any search actually performed. Note the Seller's own para 1.4 refuses to admit any matter is material or requires action – so the Seller is simultaneously disclosing everything and characterising nothing.
- **Push back:** Delete paras 1.1 and 1.2 as general disclosures. Require disclosure to be specific, with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Accept the specific disclosures (paras 2–10) only to the extent they meet that standard, and note that most of them disclose the *absence* of evidence rather than a resolved position.

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge – Clause 8.3
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier must be limited to named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Reasoning:** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard – it bars claims for matters the Buyer did *not* know but theoretically could have found. Combined with whole-data-room disclosure, this would gut the warranty package. Extending it to advisers compounds the problem.
- **Push back:** Delete Clause 8.3. If any knowledge qualifier survives, confine it to actual knowledge of named Seller individuals after reasonable enquiry, and expressly exclude title, capacity, fraud and specific indemnities.

---

## 3. Completion mechanics

### 3.1 Bluefen consent – Clause 3 / 6.3
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent. Disclosure para 2 confirms **no final written consent** and **no evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied** as at 22 September 2026.
- **Playbook:** Effective consent **and** evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Reasoning:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue. DD-002 clause 11.2 contains a change-of-control consent right and 11.3 attaches conditions. "Consent on delivery" means the condition could be ticked by a conditional or qualified letter whose conditions are never met. The Seller's description that the consent "is addressed" is contradicted by its own Disclosure Letter. The 30% concentration also makes this the single largest value risk in the deal.
- **Push back:** Condition precedent to Completion: unconditional written consent under DD-002 cl 11.2 in agreed form, together with evidence satisfactory to the Buyer that each 11.3 condition has been satisfied or irrevocably waived. Seller obligation at "all reasonable endeavours" at minimum, with Buyer approval of any conditions offered to Bluefen. If consent cannot be obtained, Buyer right not to complete (and consider a price-adjustment or escrow mechanism as a fallback, subject to deal-team instruction).

### 3.2 Riverlark facility – Clause 2 / 7
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion." Disclosure para 3 confirms not repaid, no discharge in data room.
- **Playbook:** Current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion. Post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval.
- **Reasoning:** On a debt-free/cash-free basis, a AUD 3.2m facility left outstanding at Completion with security over the Company is inconsistent with the agreed price basis. Post-completion release leaves the Buyer owning a secured company with no bank commitment to discharge. DD-003 cl 8.1 is also a change-of-control trigger – uncured, it could put the facility into default on Completion.
- **Push back:** Require (a) Riverlark payout letter dated to Completion; (b) payment direct from Completion funds to Riverlark in the funds flow; (c) executed deeds of release/discharge (PPSR, any mortgages/guarantees) delivered at Completion. Reject post-completion release unless Riverlark gives an irrevocable undertaking to release on receipt of funds and Amelia Frost approves in writing.

### 3.3 Employee bonuses – DD-005 / funds flow
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure para 5 confirms they are absent and is silent on payroll tax, super and other on-costs.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Reasoning:** These are Completion-triggered liabilities of the Company. If the funds flow omits them, the Company (and therefore the Buyer) pays them post-Completion while the Seller receives full price – an undisclosed transfer of ~AUD 420k plus on-costs (potentially superannuation and payroll tax on top). "A matter for the Seller" is a statement of intent, not a binding mechanism.
- **Push back:** Specific line item in the funds flow for AUD 420,000 **plus** all associated superannuation, payroll tax and other on-costs, deducted from the price or paid by the Seller at Completion, with a Seller indemnity for any shortfall. Request the on-cost calculation.

### 3.4 Ironquay IP – Clause 11.1
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate." Disclosure para 4: DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the room.
- **Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- **Reasoning:** The real risk is not the AUD 180,000 cash – it is that the Company may not own the SOW3 Project Materials at all until payment clears. An indemnity capped at the payment amount does not cover loss of IP ownership, third-party claims, re-development cost or Bluefen/customer consequences. The AUD 180,000 figure comes from the Company's own ledger (DD-010), not bank confirmation, so the true open amount could be different in either direction.
- **Push back:** (a) Pre-Completion: Seller to procure cleared payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees and a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay, with bank evidence of payment – this is the cure the playbook wants preserved. (b) Broaden Clause 11.1 to an indemnity for all Loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or any third-party claim to, the SOW3 Project Materials and any other Ironquay deliverables, not limited to the fee amount. (c) Request bank confirmation of the AUD 180,000.

---

## 4. Diligence matters

### 4.1 Export/privacy incident – Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (DD-006)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material. Disclosure para 6: ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) sent to an unintended external address; unknown whether accessed; notification assessment incomplete; no loss figure.
- **Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Reasoning:** Consistent with the playbook, we should not characterise this as a breach or demand a price adjustment. Equally, "not expected to be material" is the Seller's conclusion on an incomplete investigation. The Buyer needs the facts preserved and the investigation completed before Completion.
- **Push back:** Pre-Completion covenants: preserve all logs and evidence; complete the investigation (access determination, scope, notification analysis under applicable privacy law); provide written updates and the final report; specific warranty that the Disclosure Letter description is complete and accurate as updated. Consider a specific indemnity for Loss arising from the incident, scope to be settled once the investigation concludes. Do not accept the "operational matter" label in the SPA.

### 4.2 Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011) – AUD 330,000
- **Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure para 8: three renewals of AUD 110,000; disclosure does not say whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Reasoning:** We should not reflexively treat these as Debt. However, the Seller's characterisation is unsupported by its own disclosure, which expressly declines to say they are ordinary course. Timing matters: if they fall due or accrue pre-Completion, they may belong in working capital or Debt under the agreed definitions.
- **Push back:** Request the renewal terms, timing, termination rights and accrual treatment for each. Confirm treatment under the Debt / working-capital definitions once the facts are in. No concession in the SPA that they are ordinary course until assessed.

### 4.3 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- Disclosure paras 7 and 9 state that the lease has a notification obligation (not a consent) and that the Mossvale assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale. These are reasonable on their face but should be confirmed against the source documents, and the lease notification should be a pre-Completion Seller obligation with evidence of delivery.

---

## 5. Tax / IP

- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime above."
- **Playbook:** Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Reasoning:** Nothing has been agreed. The Seller's statement, read with the Clause 13 "applies to all Claims" default, would fold Tax and IP into a 20% cap and 18-month limit. That is not our position, and the playbook treats these as separate categories.
- **Push back:** Record in the issues list that Tax and IP remain open. Reject any wording that applies the general cap, basket or time limit to Tax or IP by default. Separate Tax and IP regimes to be negotiated (we should not at this stage propose unlimited liability either).

---

## 6. Title

- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012. Disclosure para 10 confirms this is the source relied on and that the Buyer has not completed independent verification.
- **Playbook:** Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Reasoning:** The share register is maintained by the Company (i.e. by the Seller's own appointees). It is not independent. In combination with the Seller's attempt to collapse Title warranties into the general regime (1.4) and Riverlark security remaining in place (3.2), title is currently under-protected on all fronts.
- **Push back:** Require independent ASIC company extract, PPSR searches against the Company and the Seller, confirmation of no security over the shares (including under the Riverlark facility), evidence of Seller's corporate authority (board/shareholder resolutions), and the full Fundamental/Title warranty regime. Buyer to complete its own verification before Completion.

---

## 7. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Revert to 25% / AUD 6.0m; 20% not authorised |
| 2 | Thresholds | AUD 25k / AUD 250k, excess only | AUD 5k / AUD 50k, first dollar |
| 3 | Time limit | 18 months; applies to all Claims by default | 24 months; delete default; limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | Separate regime: 100% cap, ≥ 6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge |
| 5 | Limitations / non-reliance | All Claims of any nature; no fraud carve-out | Confine to general Warranty Claims; express non-waivable carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct |
| 6 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public registers | Specific fair disclosure only |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket, incl. "discoverable" | Delete; any qualifier limited to named Seller persons + reasonable enquiry; never title/capacity/fraud/indemnities |
| 8 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | CP: unconditional consent + evidence 11.3 conditions satisfied before Completion |
| 9 | Riverlark | Post-completion release | Payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, releases at Completion; post-completion only with irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval |
| 10 | Bonuses | Not in funds flow | Line item: AUD 420k + on-costs, Seller-borne; indemnity |
| 11 | Ironquay | Indemnity limited to SOW3 fee | Pre-Completion cure (payment + confirmatory assignment); broaden indemnity to ownership/third-party loss; verify AUD 180k |
| 12 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | Preserve logs, complete investigation, updates; no breach assumed; specific warranty/indemnity to follow facts |
| 13 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | Assess terms and timing; no concession either way yet |
| 14 | Tax / IP | Settled under general regime | Remain OPEN; separate regimes; no default override |
| 15 | Title evidence | Internal register (DD-012) | Independent ASIC/PPSR/authority evidence; Buyer verification |

**Priority order for the mark-up / next call with Seller counsel:**
1. Fraud carve-out and Fundamental/Title separation (structural – must be fixed before anything else is meaningful).
2. Bluefen CP and Riverlark payout/release (Completion mechanics; both contradicted by Seller's own Disclosure Letter).
3. Bonus funds-flow line item and Ironquay cure (hard-dollar / IP-ownership gaps).
4. Cap, thresholds, time limit (revert to playbook; no fallback authorised).
5. Disclosure standard and Clause 8.3 knowledge bar.
6. Title evidence, DD-006 investigation, Sandbar assessment, Tax/IP flagged as open.

**Authority note:** No fallback (20% cap, 18-month period, post-completion Riverlark release) is to be offered or accepted without the specific written approval of Amelia Frost identifying the relevant draft. None exists for SPA-003.

Happy to turn this into a formal issues list or a marked-up response to Seller counsel on instruction.

- **Push back:** 24 months. Delete the "applies to all Claims" default. Replace with a clear statement that limitations in Clause 12 apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and do not apply to Fundamental/Title Warranties, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations or covenants except where that Clause expressly says so.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title warranties
- **Seller:** Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity."
- **Playbook:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside the de minimis, basket and knowledge bar.
- **Reasoning:** This is the single most important structural departure. If title fails, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for shares it may not own; a AUD 4.8m cap and 18-month window is wholly inadequate. "Administrative simplicity" is not a commercial justification. This is compounded by the fact that the Seller relies solely on its own internal register for title (see 7 below).
- **Push back:** Non-negotiable. Separate Fundamental/Title regime per playbook.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance – Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5
- **Seller:** Apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- **Reasoning:** The draft contains no fraud carve-out at all. "All Claims of any nature" would, on its face, cap and time-bar fraud and apply non-reliance to deliberately misleading statements. Apart from being unacceptable commercially, provisions purporting to exclude liability for fraud are of doubtful enforceability and invite dispute. The exclusive-remedy clause applied to "all Claims" would also bar claims under specific indemnities, covenants and the payment mechanics.
- **Push back:** Insert express fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out from every limitation, the exclusive-remedy clause and non-reliance. Limit the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions to general Warranty Claims only. Confirm the carve-out cannot be waived.

## 2. Disclosure and Buyer knowledge

### 2.1 Disclosure – Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."
- **Playbook:** Require specific, fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Reasoning:** Blanket data-room disclosure shifts the risk of every document in the room to the Buyer regardless of whether the relevant issue was fairly identified. Public-register disclosure is open-ended and not tied to any search actually performed. Note the Seller's own para 1.4 refuses to admit any matter is material or requires action – so the Seller is simultaneously disclosing everything and characterising nothing.
- **Push back:** Delete paras 1.1 and 1.2 as general disclosures. Require disclosure to be specific, with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter. Accept the specific disclosures (paras 2–10) only to the extent they meet that standard, and note that most of them disclose the *absence* of evidence rather than a resolved position.

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge – Clause 8.3
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier must be limited to named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Reasoning:** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard – it bars claims for matters the Buyer did *not* know but theoretically could have found. Combined with whole-data-room disclosure, this would gut the warranty package. Extending it to advisers compounds the problem.
- **Push back:** Delete Clause 8.3. If any knowledge qualifier survives, confine it to actual knowledge of named Seller individuals after reasonable enquiry, and expressly exclude title, capacity, fraud and specific indemnities.

## 3. Completion mechanics

### 3.1 Bluefen consent – Clause 3 / 6.3
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent. Disclosure para 2 confirms **no final written consent** and **no evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied** as at 22 September 2026.
- **Playbook:** Effective consent **and** evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Reasoning:** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue. DD-002 clause 11.2 contains a change-of-control consent right and 11.3 attaches conditions. "Consent on delivery" means the condition could be ticked by a conditional or qualified letter whose conditions are never met. The Seller's description that the consent "is addressed" is contradicted by its own Disclosure Letter. The 30% concentration also makes this the single largest value risk in the deal.
- **Push back:** Condition precedent to Completion: unconditional written consent under DD-002 cl 11.2 in agreed form, together with evidence satisfactory to the Buyer that each 11.3 condition has been satisfied or irrevocably waived. Seller obligation at "all reasonable endeavours" at minimum, with Buyer approval of any conditions offered to Bluefen. If consent cannot be obtained, Buyer right not to complete (and consider a price-adjustment or escrow mechanism as a fallback, subject to deal-team instruction).

### 3.2 Riverlark facility – Clause 2 / 7
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion." Disclosure para 3 confirms not repaid, no discharge in data room.
- **Playbook:** Current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion. Post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval.
- **Reasoning:** On a debt-free/cash-free basis, a AUD 3.2m facility left outstanding at Completion with security over the Company is inconsistent with the agreed price basis. Post-completion release leaves the Buyer owning a secured company with no bank commitment to discharge. DD-003 cl 8.1 is also a change-of-control trigger – uncured, it could put the facility into default on Completion.
- **Push back:** Require (a) Riverlark payout letter dated to Completion; (b) payment direct from Completion funds to Riverlark in the funds flow; (c) executed deeds of release/discharge (PPSR, any mortgages/guarantees) delivered at Completion. Reject post-completion release unless Riverlark gives an irrevocable undertaking to release on receipt of funds and Amelia Frost approves in writing.

### 3.3 Employee bonuses – DD-005 / funds flow
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure para 5 confirms they are absent and is silent on payroll tax, super and other on-costs.
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Reasoning:** These are Completion-triggered liabilities of the Company. If the funds flow omits them, the Company (and therefore the Buyer) pays them post-Completion while the Seller receives full price – an undisclosed transfer of ~AUD 420k plus on-costs (potentially superannuation and payroll tax on top). "A matter for the Seller" is a statement of intent, not a binding mechanism.
- **Push back:** Specific line item in the funds flow for AUD 420,000 **plus** all associated superannuation, payroll tax and other on-costs, deducted from the price or paid by the Seller at Completion, with a Seller indemnity for any shortfall. Request the on-cost calculation.

### 3.4 Ironquay IP – Clause 11.1
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate." Disclosure para 4: DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the room.
- **Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- **Reasoning:** The real risk is not the AUD 180,000 cash – it is that the Company may not own the SOW3 Project Materials at all until payment clears. An indemnity capped at the payment amount does not cover loss of IP ownership, third-party claims, re-development cost or Bluefen/customer consequences. The AUD 180,000 figure comes from the Company's own ledger (DD-010), not bank confirmation, so the true open amount could be different in either direction.
- **Push back:** (a) Pre-Completion: Seller to procure cleared payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees and a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay, with bank evidence of payment – this is the cure the playbook wants preserved. (b) Broaden Clause 11.1 to an indemnity for all Loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or any third-party claim to, the SOW3 Project Materials and any other Ironquay deliverables, not limited to the fee amount. (c) Request bank confirmation of the AUD 180,000.

## 4. Diligence matters

### 4.1 Export/privacy incident – Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (DD-006)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material. Disclosure para 6: ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) sent to an unintended external address; unknown whether accessed; notification assessment incomplete; no loss figure.
- **Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume **no** confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Reasoning:** Consistent with the playbook, we should not characterise this as a breach or demand a price adjustment. Equally, "not expected to be material" is the Seller's conclusion on an incomplete investigation. The Buyer needs the facts preserved and the investigation completed before Completion.
- **Push back:** Pre-Completion covenants: preserve all logs and evidence; complete the investigation (access determination, scope, notification analysis under applicable privacy law); provide written updates and the final report; specific warranty that the Disclosure Letter description is complete and accurate as updated. Consider a specific indemnity for Loss arising from the incident, scope to be settled once the investigation concludes. Do not accept the "operational matter" label in the SPA.

### 4.2 Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011) – AUD 330,000
- **Seller:** Ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure para 8: three renewals of AUD 110,000; disclosure does not say whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Reasoning:** We should not reflexively treat these as Debt. However, the Seller's characterisation is unsupported by its own disclosure, which expressly declines to say they are ordinary course. Timing matters: if they fall due or accrue pre-Completion, they may belong in working capital or Debt under the agreed definitions.
- **Push back:** Request the renewal terms, timing, termination rights and accrual treatment for each. Confirm treatment under the Debt / working-capital definitions once the facts are in. No concession in the SPA that they are ordinary course until assessed.

### 4.3 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- Disclosure paras 7 and 9 state that the lease has a notification obligation (not a consent) and that the Mossvale assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale. These are reasonable on their face but should be confirmed against the source documents, and the lease notification should be a pre-Completion Seller obligation with evidence of delivery.

## 6. Title

- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the share register at DD-012. Disclosure para 10 confirms this is the source relied on and that the Buyer has not completed independent verification.
- **Playbook:** Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Reasoning:** The share register is maintained by the Company (i.e. by the Seller's own appointees). It is not independent. In combination with the Seller's attempt to collapse Title warranties into the general regime (1.4) and Riverlark security remaining in place (3.2), title is currently under-protected on all fronts.
- **Push back:** Require independent ASIC company extract, PPSR searches against the Company and the Seller, confirmation of no security over the shares (including under the Riverlark facility), evidence of Seller's corporate authority (board/shareholder resolutions), and the full Fundamental/Title warranty regime. Buyer to complete its own verification before Completion.
